findings.description: The inline policy grants full wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) against "Resource": "*", which is effectively administrative control over compute, storage, serverless, and monitoring in the account. Any compromise of this user's static key yields the ability to read/delete all S3 data, launch or terminate instances, and modify Lambda code.

A permanent IAM access key is created for the user with no pgp_key set, so the plaintext secret access key is written into Terraform state and never rotated. Static keys attached to users persist until manually revoked and should be replaced by federated/temporary credentials via IAM roles.

The output "secret" exports the access key's secret attribute. Because no pgp_key was supplied, encrypted_secret is unpopulated and the credential material is recorded in the Terraform state/output store in clear text, readable by anyone with state or `terraform output` access.
The IAM user receives a highly privileged inline policy directly with no permissions_boundary and no group-based assignment, so there is no guardrail limiting escalation of its effective privileges.
